ei.title: 8번: A Man and a Penguin's Annual Reunion
ei.subject: 빠른독해바른독해_구문독해_2024

fullPassage: In 2011, Joao Pereira de Souza, an old man living in an island village near Rio de Janeiro, Brazil, found a penguin struggling on the beach. The helpless, starving creature covered in oil was adopted by Mr. de Souza and named Dindim. Mr. de Souza nursed him back to health and released him, thinking they would never meet again. Amazingly, though, Dindim returned! It is believed that he traveled around 5,000 miles between Mr. de Souza's house and the coasts of Argentina and Chile. What is more, he makes this journey every year. After spending about eight months with Mr. de Souza, he goes on his annual migration for his breeding routine, only to return once again.

questions.passage: In 2011, Joao Pereira de Souza, an old man living in an island village near Rio de Janeiro, Brazil, found a penguin (A)[struggling / resting] on the beach. The helpless, starving creature covered in oil was adopted by Mr. de Souza and named Dindim. Mr. de Souza (B)[neglected / nursed] him back to health and released him, thinking they would never meet again. Amazingly, though, Dindim (C)[returned / vanished]! It is believed that he traveled around 5,000 miles between Mr. de Souza's house and the coasts of Argentina and Chile. What is more, he makes this journey every year. After spending about eight months with Mr. de Souza, he goes on his annual migration for his breeding routine, only to return once again.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: (A) struggling=고군분투하는 / resting=쉬는 (B) nursed=간호했다 / neglected=방치했다 (C) returned=돌아왔다 / vanished=사라졌다
det.analysis:
① struggling — nursed — returned: 해변에서 고군분투하는 펭귄, 건강하게 간호해 주었고, 놀랍게도 다시 돌아왔다 ←정답
② resting: 무력하게 애쓰는 상황이므로 '쉬는(resting)'은 부적절
③ vanished: 'Amazingly, though'(놀랍게도) 뒤에는 돌아왔다(returned)가 자연스러움
④ resting/vanished: 모두 문맥과 반대
det.tip: 펭귄이 애쓰다(struggling) → 간호받고(nursed) → 돌아옴(returned)의 흐름

questions.passage: In 2011, Joao Pereira de Souza, an old man living in an island village near Rio de Janeiro, Brazil, found a penguin struggling on the beach. The (A)[helpless / powerful], starving creature covered in oil was adopted by Mr. de Souza and named Dindim. Mr. de Souza nursed him back to health and released him, thinking they would never meet again. Amazingly, though, Dindim returned! It is believed that he (B)[remained / traveled] around 5,000 miles between Mr. de Souza's house and the coasts of Argentina and Chile. What is more, he makes this journey every year. After spending about eight months with Mr. de Souza, he goes on his (C)[annual / occasional] migration for his breeding routine, only to return once again.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: (A) helpless=무력한 / powerful=강력한 (B) traveled=이동했다 / remained=머물렀다 (C) annual=매년의 / occasional=가끔의
det.analysis:
① powerful: 기름을 뒤집어쓰고 굶주린 생명체는 강력한(powerful) 것이 아니라 무력한(helpless)
② remained/occasional: 5,000마일을 이동(traveled)했고 매년(annual) 반복함
③ helpless — traveled — annual: 무력한 생명체, 5,000마일 이동, 매년의 이동 ←정답
④ powerful: (A) 문맥과 반대
det.tip: 굶주린 생명체=helpless, 5,000마일=traveled, 매년 반복=annual

questions.passage: In 2011, Joao Pereira de Souza, an old man living in an island village near Rio de Janeiro, Brazil, found a penguin struggling on the beach. The helpless, (A)[starving / well-fed] creature covered in oil was (B)[abandoned / adopted] by Mr. de Souza and named Dindim. Mr. de Souza nursed him back to health and released him, thinking they would never meet again. Amazingly, though, Dindim returned! It is believed that he traveled around 5,000 miles between Mr. de Souza's house and the coasts of Argentina and Chile. What is more, he makes this journey every year. After spending about eight months with Mr. de Souza, he goes on his annual migration for his (C)[feeding / breeding] routine, only to return once again.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: (A) starving=굶주린 / well-fed=잘 먹은 (B) adopted=거두었다 / abandoned=버렸다 (C) breeding=번식 / feeding=먹이 주기
det.analysis:
① starving — adopted — breeding: 굶주린 생명체를 de Souza가 거두었고, 번식을 위한 이동을 함 ←정답
② well-fed/abandoned: 기름을 뒤집어쓴 채 발견되었으므로 굶주린(starving) 상태, 이름을 지어줬으니 거둔(adopted) 것
③ feeding: 매년 이주 목적은 먹이가 아니라 번식(breeding)
④ well-fed/feeding: 모두 문맥과 반대
det.tip: 굶주린(starving) 펭귄을 거두고(adopted), 번식(breeding)을 위해 이주

questions.passage: In 2011, Joao Pereira de Souza, an old man living in an island village near Rio de Janeiro, Brazil, found a penguin ①<u>struggling</u> on the beach. The helpless, starving creature covered in oil was ②<u>adopted</u> by Mr. de Souza and named Dindim. Mr. de Souza nursed him back to health and ③<u>captured</u> him, thinking they would never meet again. Amazingly, though, Dindim returned! It is believed that he traveled around 5,000 miles between Mr. de Souza's house and the coasts of Argentina and Chile. What is more, he makes this journey every year. After spending about eight months with Mr. de Souza, he goes on his ④<u>annual</u> migration for his breeding routine, only to return once again.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ① struggling=고군분투하는 ② adopted=거두어진 ③ captured→released(풀어주다) ④ annual=매년의
det.analysis:
① struggling: 해변에서 애쓰는 펭귄 — 적절
② adopted: de Souza에게 거두어짐 — 적절
③ captured: 건강하게 돌본 뒤 '가두었다'? 다시 못 만날 거라 했으니 풀어준(released) 것 ←정답
④ annual: 매년의 이주 — 적절
det.tip: 다시 못 만날 거라 생각한 이유 = 풀어줬기(released) 때문. captured(가두다)는 반대

det.korean: ① powerful→helpless(무력한) ② traveled=이동했다 ③ journey=여정 ④ breeding=번식
det.analysis:

② traveled: 5,000마일을 이동 — 적절
③ journey: 이 여정을 매년 함 — 적절
④ breeding: 번식을 위한 이주 — 적절
det.tip: 굶주려 기름을 뒤집어쓴 펭귄 = helpless(무력한). powerful(강력한)은 반대

det.korean: ① creature=생명체 ② disappeared→returned(돌아왔다) ③ traveled=이동했다 ④ migration=이주
det.analysis:

questions.passage:
(A) His morning <u>routine</u> never changes: he wakes up at six, drinks a cup of coffee, and reads the news before going to work.

(B) The doctor told us that the surgery was a completely <u>routine</u> operation, so there was really nothing for us to worry about.
questions.stem: 다음 (A)와 (B)에서 밑줄 친 routine의 의미로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: routine: (A) 규칙적으로 반복되는 일과(명사) (B) 평범한, 특별할 것 없는(형용사)
det.analysis:
① (A)를 '평범한'으로 본 것은 오류 — morning routine은 매일 반복되는 일과
② (A) 규칙적으로 반복되는 일과 (B) 평범한: morning routine=아침 일과, routine operation=특별할 것 없는 수술 ←정답
③ (B)를 '힘들고 위험한'으로 본 것은 오류 — routine operation은 걱정할 것 없는 수술
④ (A)를 '갑작스러운'으로 본 것은 오류
det.tip: routine = 명사(반복되는 일과) vs 형용사(평범한, 일상적인)의 다의어

questions.stem: 다음 영영 정의에 해당하는 단어로 가장 적절한 것은? "the regular seasonal movement of animals from one place to another"

det.korean: hibernation=동면 / celebration=축하 / education=교육 / migration=이주, 이동
det.analysis:
① hibernation: 동면 — 겨울잠이지 이동이 아님
② celebration: 축하 — 의미 다름
③ education: 교육 — 의미 다름
④ migration: 동물이 한 장소에서 다른 장소로 규칙적으로 계절에 따라 이동하는 것 ←정답
det.tip: seasonal movement of animals(동물의 계절 이동) = migration(이주)

questions.passage: Amazingly, though, Dindim returned! It is believed that he __________ (travel) around 5,000 miles between Mr. de Souza's house and the coasts of Argentina and Chile.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (영어로)

det.korean: travel(동사: 이동하다) → traveled(과거형: 이동했다). 이미 일어난 일이므로 과거시제
det.analysis: travel을 과거형 traveled로 변환. 'It is believed that he traveled'는 그가 이미 5,000마일을 이동했다고 믿어진다는 뜻으로, 이미 일어난 일이므로 과거시제가 필요
det.tip: 돌아온(returned) 뒤 이동했음을 서술 → 과거시제 traveled

questions.passage: What is more, he makes this journey every year. After __________ (spend) about eight months with Mr. de Souza, he goes on his annual migration for his breeding routine, only to return once again.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (영어로)

det.korean: spend(동사: 보내다) → spending(동명사). 전치사 After 뒤에는 동명사(-ing)가 옴
det.analysis: spend를 동명사 spending으로 변환. 'After spending about eight months'는 '약 8개월을 보낸 후에'라는 뜻으로, 전치사 After 다음에는 명사 역할을 하는 동명사(-ing) 형태가 필요
det.tip: 전치사(After) + 동명사(-ing). After spending = ~을 보낸 후에

questions.passage: In 2011, Joao Pereira de Souza, an old man living in an island village near Rio de Janeiro, Brazil, found a penguin struggling on the beach. The helpless, starving creature covered in oil was adopted by Mr. de Souza and named Dindim. Mr. de Souza nursed him __________ and released him, thinking they would never meet again. Amazingly, though, Dindim returned! It is believed that he traveled around 5,000 miles between Mr. de Souza's house and the coasts of Argentina and Chile. What is more, he makes this journey every year. After spending about eight months with Mr. de Souza, he goes on his annual migration for his breeding routine, only to return once again.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: to the village=마을로 / back to health=건강하게(원래대로) / into the sea=바다로 / away from home=집에서 멀리
det.analysis:
① to the village: 마을로 돌보다? 어색함
② back to health: 굶주리고 병든 펭귄을 간호해 건강을 회복시킴 ←정답
③ into the sea: 아직 풀어주기 전 단계 — 부적절
④ away from home: 집에서 멀리 돌보다? 문맥 부적절
det.tip: nursed him ______(간호하다) + 이후 풀어줌 → back to health(건강하게 회복시켜)

questions.passage: In 2011, Joao Pereira de Souza, an old man living in an island village near Rio de Janeiro, Brazil, found a penguin struggling on the beach. The helpless, starving creature covered in oil was adopted by Mr. de Souza and named Dindim. Mr. de Souza nursed him back to health and released him, thinking they would never meet again. Amazingly, though, Dindim returned! It is believed that he traveled around 5,000 miles between Mr. de Souza's house and the coasts of Argentina and Chile. What is more, he makes this journey every year. After spending about eight months with Mr. de Souza, he goes on his annual migration for his breeding routine, __________.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: never to be seen again=다시는 볼 수 없게 / hoping to escape the cold=추위를 피하려고 / only to return once again=결국 다시 돌아오려고 / trying to find a new home=새 보금자리를 찾으려고
det.analysis:
① never to be seen again: 매년 돌아오므로(every year) 부적절
② hoping to escape the cold: 목적은 번식(breeding)이지 추위가 아님
③ only to return once again: 번식 이주를 떠나지만 결국 매년 다시 돌아옴 ←정답
④ trying to find a new home: 새 집을 찾는 것이 아니라 de Souza에게 돌아옴
det.tip: 매년 반복되는 재회 이야기 → 이주를 떠나도 결국 다시 돌아옴(return once again)

ch: trying to find a new home
